column1: # sm_89 (Ada) memory-op load-use latency, per space and global cache tier.
# Method.  Single-warp clock64 pointer-chase: each memory op's address is a
# strict data-dependency on the prior op's loaded value, so the SM cannot hide
# the latency behind ILP and the per-op cycle count IS the load-use latency.
# clock64 (SR_CLOCKLO) counts SM cycles independent of the boost clock, so the
# figures are clock-invariant.  Global cache tiers are isolated by sizing the
# chase working set against the Ada hierarchy (L1 <= 128 KiB/SM, L2 = 24 MiB on
# this part): 2 KiB set -> L1-hit, 1 MiB -> L2, 96 MiB -> DRAM miss.  Each value
# is the median of 7 launches x 4096 dependent ops (run-to-run spread < 1%).
# Scoreboard mechanism (decoded from ptxas-emitted SASS, CUDA 13.1).  Every load
# is DECOUPLED: it issues, arms a WRITE scoreboard (the SASS dst_wr_sb field,
# bits 110-112), and retires asynchronously.  The dependent consumer carries
# that scoreboard id in its read-barrier wait mask (req_bit_set, bits 116-121)
# and blocks until the load's write scoreboard clears.  ptxas alternates the two
# long-scoreboards (SB2/SB5 in the sm_89 scoreboard config) across back-to-back
# loads.  The instruction's static usched stall (bits 105-109) is an ISSUE-
# THROUGHPUT hint only -- NOT the load latency: patching a consumer load's
# usched stall down to 1 while keeping its scoreboard wait leaves the result
# bit-identical and the measured stall unchanged, because the Volta-class SM
# hardware-interlocks the dependent register read on the producer's write
# scoreboard regardless of the static stall value.  The flat worst-case "300"
# band ptxas assumes for a global load is purely a critical-path WEIGHT for
# scheduling; the runtime stall is whatever the scoreboard takes to clear, which
# is the cache-tier-dependent latency tabulated below.
# source_model = the CUDA-13 ptxas scheduler-model figure for the op: the MIO/
# AGU pipe issue-occupancy (mio_pipe = 18) for the throughput term, the ptxas
# L2-miss-path latency input (~150 cycles) for the L2 tier, and the worst-case
# scoreboard band (300) ptxas weights an un-analyzable global load with.  These
# are static model inputs; the gpu_measured_latency column is the silicon truth.
# Columns: op  space  cache_tier  sets_scoreboard  source_model  gpu_measured_latency  note
